claims.text: Plasma nitriding Ti-6Al-4V at 500–550 °C for 6–10 hours with a controlled N2/H2 mixture will form a nitrided surface layer.
The nitrided surface layer will be composed primarily of TiN and Ti2N phases.
The resulting nitride layer will be well-adherent.
The resulting nitride layer will retain sufficient ductility under cyclic loading.
Optimized plasma nitriding will increase Ti-6Al-4V surface hardness by 50–100% relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Optimized plasma nitriding will significantly improve wear resistance under cyclic sliding and abrasive wear conditions relative to untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Nitrogen atoms diffuse into the Ti-6Al-4V surface during plasma nitriding.
Diffused nitrogen reacts with titanium to form hard titanium nitride phases.
Controlling treatment temperature, duration, and N2/H2 ratio can limit excessive brittleness in the nitrided layer.
Maintaining sufficient layer ductility will reduce brittleness and spallation during cyclic loading.
Poor adhesion or spallation would indicate that the treatment produced an excessively brittle or otherwise inadequate layer.
Variations in the initial Ti-6Al-4V microstructure may influence treatment outcomes.
Process scalability may influence the resulting hardness, layer integrity, or wear performance.
